rules.name: apply_patch edit extraction
rules.trigger: tool.execute.after / PostToolUse where tool is apply_patch; checker extracts changed-file edits before/after so the binary can compare added vs existing code
rules.behavior: extractApplyPatchEdits reads file metadata from details.files / result.files / metadata.files (types  not delete), else parses the '*** Add/Update/Delete File:' + '*** Move to:' patch protocol with @@ context and +/− markers into CheckerEdit[] {filePath, before, after}. Add-file edits have before=''. Delete files are filtered out because they cannot introduce new comments.

rules.name: write/edit/multiedit coverage
rules.trigger: PostToolUse after a successful write, edit, multiedit (or multi_edit); the tool must be edit-like
rules.behavior: extractCommentCheckRequests maps the tool to a CommentCheckRequest with tool_name Write/Edit/MultiEdit and a matching toolInput (content / old_string+new_string / edits[]). Non-edit tools return []. Tool failures (output text starts with 'error', contains 'error:', 'failed to', 'could not') are ignored so the checker never evaluates failed edits.

rules.name: report-only (no code mutation)
rules.behavior: The checker only reports: core runner returns CheckResult {hasComments, message}; opencode consumer appends the message to the tool's output string without touching the file, and the codex consumer returns a JSON {decision:'block', reason:...} so the MODEL fixes or explains the flagged comment. No CheckerEdit is ever applied back to disk by this pipeline.

rules.name: exit-code contract
rules.trigger: subprocess exits: 0 / 2 / other / timeout / missing binary
rules.behavior: exit 0 => clean EMPTY_RESULT {hasComments:false}. exit 2 => {hasComments:true, message:stderr} (the flagged-comments report). Any other exit code, spawning error, or timeout silently returns EMPTY_RESULT (no warning). Missing/unusable binary returns EMPTY_RESULT from the start.

rules.name: net-new comment filter
rules.trigger: edit with oldString and newString (write/apply_patch caller path)
rules.behavior: Comment warnings are only emitted for edits that introduce NET-NEW comment syntax. hasNewCommentsOnly compares oldText/newText at line level; if the same comment already existed in oldString it is skipped (reduces false positives for in-place comment tweaks). Pure add-file content is treated as all-new by definition.

rules.name: per-session dedup
rules.behavior: At most one comment warning is emitted per session within a 30s dedup window, to prevent a deadloop where repeatedly re-introducing a comment re-warns each turn.

rules.name: missing / unscopable binary is silent
rules.trigger: binary path null or non-existent; also remote HTTP skill sources
rules.behavior: Both editions emit no hook output when the @code-yeongyu/comment-checker binary cannot be resolved or is missing on the current platform, so agents keep working. Binary resolution prefers a cached path, then createRequire(package)/bin/<name>, then PATH lookup; opencode edition also lazily downloads it.

rules.name: bounded feedback / context protection
rules.trigger: checker produces a long warning, or transcript shows context pressure
rules.behavior: Codex hook caps hook feedback at 8000 chars normally, 1200 chars when the transcript contains context-compaction markers, truncating with a marker note to avoid overflowing the model context.

notes: comment-checker-core (packages/comment-checker-core/, src and tests ONLY) is a parser + subprocess runner: it parses apply_patch edits into CheckerEdit[] and pipes HookInput JSON to the external @code-yeongyu/comment-checker Go binary, then maps exit codes to CheckResult. It does NOT contain the pattern-level rules themselves (comment-sync check, banned comment patterns, TODO/assertion rules). Those live inside the external '@code-yeongyu/comment-checker' binary (github.com/code-yeongyu/go-claude-code-comment-checker), which is NOT in this source tree — so those specific rules were not extractable from the scoped directory and are not fabricated here.

The comment checker does NOT auto-fix or modify code comments; it only reports (appends/returns a warning) so the model corrects or explains it. autoFixesCode=false is grounded at runner.ts:53-123, cli-runner.ts:119-124, and codex-hook.ts:73-79.

Hashline association: comment-checker and hashline are UNRELATED modules. comment-checker-core and its consumers contain zero references to hashline; packages/hashline-core contains zero references to comment-checker. They coexist only as independent post-tool hooks in the same opencode pipeline (see omo-opencode/src/plugin/AGENTS.md:22). The AGENTS.md line lists 'truncation, comment-checker, hashline read tagging' as separate 'tool.execute.after' hooks.

The single test file in comment-checker-core (apply-patch-edits.test.ts, 29 lines) only validates legacy record semantics of getApplyPatchMetadataFiles accepting an array wrapper with a .files property.

resolveCommentCheckerBinary accepts a packageName override but defaults to '@code-yeongyu/comment-checker'; the actual binary name is platform-dependent (comment-checker.exe on win32 else comment-checker).

facts.fact: Four-to-seven discovery scopes are enumerated by source locations and each LoadedSkill carries a 'scope'. Merger SCOPE_PRIORITY (highest win): opencode-project=6 > project=5 > opencode=4 > user=3 > config=2 > shared=1 = builtin=1.
Same-named skill at a higher scope overrides lower; mergeSkills iterates all fileSystem skills and only replaces when the incoming skill's scope priority is strictly greater than the existing one.

Project skill dirs are discovered by walking ancestors from the working directory up to the git worktree top: <.claude/skills> (scope 'project'), <.agents/skills> (scope 'project'), and <.opencode/skills> + <.opencode/skill> (scope 'opencode-project').

User scopes: Claude user skills dir = getClaudeConfigDir()/skills with scope 'user'; agents global = ~/.agents/skills with scope 'user'; opencode global = getOpenCodeSkillDirs({binary:'opencode'}) with scope 'opencode'.
Shared/built-in scope: shared skillsRootPath() loaded with scope 'shared'; the ~12 built-in skills (git-master, playwright, frontend, review-work, etc.) are created as scope 'builtin'.

discoverAllSkills aggregate order: opencodeProject, opencodeGlobal, project(Claude), agentsProject, user(Claude), agentsGlobal, shared, then deduplicateSkillsByName keeps the FIRST occurrence — since scope priority dedup is applied by merger/mergeSkills in the runtime path, caller order plus explicit priority drives the effective winner.

Disable-list semantics: config `skills.disable` array, config entries with value false, and entries with `disable:true` are all collected (names lower-cased) into a disabled set and removed from the final skill map. A nested `disabled_skills` array is also honored (skill-disable-config.ts).
Enable-list semantics: if config `skills.enable` is non-empty, only skills whose name is in the enable set are retained (everything else deleted) — an allowlist that acts after disable handling.

Config boolean entries: `entry: true` is a no-op marker that adds nothing by itself; `entry: false` deletes the skill and also deletes it even when a per-name isConfigEntryAllowed gate would skip it (delete runs even for disallowed names).

Config object entries define skills inline via description/template/model/agent/subtask; `from:` loads an .md file inside the project root (rejected with a log if outside); `template:` without `from` is allowed; entries with neither produce null. All config entries are normalized to scope 'config'.

Category association: the skills loader does NOT assign skills to categories. 'category' appears only inside team-mode / task-related builtin-skill CONTENT (team-mode.ts, security-research SKILL.md) describing worker categories like quick/deep/ultrabrain, and skills are referenced from tasks via `load_skills=[...]`, not by a skill<->category rule in the loader. Project-skill-tool-references.test.ts asserts skills delegate via real tool names and do not fabricate a task category.

Loading semantics: skills are discovered, parsed (YAML frontmatter + body), and rendered into CommandDefinition templates wrapped as <skill-instruction>...<user-request>$ARGUMENTS</user-request>. They are invoked EXPLICITLY — via getSkillByName/matchSkillByName lookup or slash-command/style loading (and referenced through load_skills in task calls) — they are NOT auto-injected into every model turn as always-on instructions; built-in skills may still be auto-exposed as skill commands.

Skill name conflict resolution on lookup: matchSkillByName first tries exact (case-insensitive) name; if exactly one skill has that short name after the last '/' it also matches that short name; `matchCommandByName` sorts by scope priority (project=4 > user=3 > opencode=2 > opencode-project=2 > shared/plugin/config/builtin=1) and returns the first exact name match.

Discovery depth/recursion: directory skills loaded from a dir tree (SKILL.md or <name>.md, max nested depth 2 in async-loader); config `sources` may be a path (optionally recursive up to MAX_RECURSIVE_DEPTH=10) or glob-filtered, or a single .md file; HTTP(s) source URLs are ignored (return empty).

Provider-gated built-in skills: skills named agent-browser or playwright are only kept in the merged list when their name equals the selected browserProvider (default 'playwright'); otherwise discovered duplicates are filtered out and builtins for non-matching providers are skipped.

A per-call result cache (keyed by directory+browserProvider+teamMode) is used for getAllSkills; the cache is bypassed whenever a non-empty disabledSkills set is passed to avoid stale disable results. Cached lists are stored even without disable filtering.
opencode config can add skill sources via `skills.paths` and `skills.urls` arrays in .opencode/opencode.json(.c) and global config; paths/urls are collected with de-dup across matching config files.

notes: skills-loader-core (packages/skills-loader-core/, src and tests) is a harness-neutral skill DISCOVERY + MATCHING + MERGE layer; it does not itself read the file system for 'shipped/deployment' skills beyond the shared/builtin scopes, so the 'shipped' layer maps to the builtin ('builtin' scope) and shared ('shared' scope) sources here, both at priority 1 (lowest).

Two distinct SCOPE_PRIORITY tables exist: the merger uses builtin=1,shared=1,config=2,user=3,opencode=4,project=5,opencode-project=6 (merger/scope-priority.ts); the tools/skill matcher uses a slightly different table (project=4,user=3,opencode=2,opencode-project=2,shared=1,plugin=1,config=1,builtin=1). Do not mix them when reasoning about precedence; the merger table governs the runtime merged skill list, the matcher table governs /command lookup sorting.

Disable semantics use lower-cased alias matching, and a disabled/empty-name entry does not delete every matching alias of the same normalized name only (see isDisabledAlias — exact normalized compare, not partial).

About 'hashline' for the skills loader: no reference to hashline exists in skills-loader-core; hashline is an unrelated hash-anchored edit tool (packages/hashline-core), not part of skill discovery/loading.
Facts are grounded in src/*.ts files under packages/skills-loader-core and its tests; line numbers refer to relative paths within that package except where a ../omo-codex path prefix is present.

extractionNotes: Task scope honored: comment-checker extracted from packages/comment-checker-core/ (src + tests) with consumers referenced where behavior (report-only, codex block decision) is defined outside the core package; skills-loader extracted from packages/skills-loader-core/ (src + tests).

autoFixesCode: The comment checker NEVER auto-modifies code comments; it only reports (appends warning / returns block decision) for the model to act on. Confirmed at comment-checker-core runner.ts:53-123, omo-opencode cli-runner.ts:119-124, and omo-codex codex-hook.ts:73-79.

Hashline: comment-checker and hashline are NOT associated. No cross-reference exists in either module's source. They only share the same tool.execute.after hook pipeline (see omo-opencode/src/plugin/AGENTS.md:22).

Skill discovery order (its own concrete scopes): opencode-project(6) > project(5) > opencode(4) > user(3) > config(2) > shared/builtin(1). The task's user/project/shipped phrasing maps to: user=user scope, project=project/opencode-project scopes, shipped=shared+builtin scopes (lowest priority).

The pattern-level comment rules that the question guessed at (comment-sync-after-edit, banned comment patterns, TODO/assertion rules) are NOT in the scoped comment-checker-core; they are implemented in the external '@code-yeongyu/comment-checker' Go binary which is not in this source tree. They were therefore recorded in notes and reported as not found rather than fabricated, per instructions.
All JSON field line sources were verified against the actual checked-out source (read tool), with ../omo-opencode and ../omo-codex prefixes used for consumer files outside the two scoped packages.
